mission: The SurveillanceDroneSwarm holds continuous watch over a tasked area of up to 25 km² for an operations centre: it takes tasking, supervisory command, recall and report acknowledgement from the centre and what its sensors see of the area, and returns triaged detection reports, correlated tracks, decision records and a status picture, while constrained by airspace clearance, radio interference, satellite-positioning outages, weather and a fleet of twelve drones, and supplied by a mesh radio, a ground-station link, a battery-swap ground crew and stored maps.
functionSentence: SurveillanceDroneSwarm carries the tasked area from unwatched and unreported to continuously watched with acknowledged detection reports at the operations centre.

stakeholders.name: OperationsCentreAnalyst
stakeholders.role: Watches the feeds and reports, judges what matters, acknowledges each detection report; the one whose attention the triage has to protect.

stakeholders.name: DutyController
stakeholders.role: Today assigns sectors, hands sectors over, re-spreads assets, keeps them apart and relays reports by hand; the operational entity's supervisor, and the role the swarm's coordination takes over.

stakeholders.name: SwarmSupervisor
stakeholders.role: The single operator who tasks, commands, recalls and watches the whole swarm rather than flying each drone.

stakeholders.name: AirspaceAuthority
stakeholders.role: Clears when and where anything may fly; its geofence and window constrain every sortie.

stakeholders.name: GroundCrew
stakeholders.role: Services drones between sorties and swaps batteries at the recharge point in about twenty minutes.

stakeholders.name: FixedCameraNetworkOperator
stakeholders.role: Keeps the existing camera network and its own tracks; what the swarm reports is merged with those tracks at the operations centre.

stakeholders.name: ProcuringCustomer
stakeholders.role: Fields the twelve drones, states the numbers still marked placeholder, and chooses between the ground-centred and drone-centred architectures.

stakeholders.name: SafetyAuthority
stakeholders.role: Holds the swarm to the rules it never breaks — recall, geofence, return when isolated, quarantine — enforced by something independent of the detection software.

environment.name: MissionTasking
environment.doc: The area of interest, its sectors and the mission window, issued by the operations centre.

environment.name: SupervisoryCommand
environment.doc: Priorities, a sector to look at more closely, and the reporting threshold — the least confidence a classification needs before it becomes a report.

environment.name: RecallOrder
environment.doc: An order to recall and land the whole swarm or one drone, arriving at any time.

environment.name: ReportAcknowledgement
environment.doc: The operations centre confirming each detection report, so nothing is lost in a link gap.

environment.name: MovingObjectsInArea
environment.doc: The objects in the watched area that have to be detected, classified and reported — the thing the mission is about.

environment.name: SceneConditions
environment.doc: Lighting, weather and deliberately misleading paint or shapes, which degrade what the sensors can tell apart.

environment.name: DetectionReports
environment.doc: Position, time, class, confidence and provenance for each detected object, delivered to the operations centre.

environment.name: CorrelatedTracks
environment.doc: One track per object rather than one per observing drone, for merging with the fixed camera network's tracks at the operations centre.

environment.name: TriagedAlertStream
environment.doc: What is most likely to matter, first, with duplicates merged, sized to what one operator can judge.

environment.name: StatusPicture
environment.doc: Where every drone is, what it is doing, how much coverage there is and what is degraded.

environment.name: DecisionRecord
environment.doc: For every report: the frames it came from, the classifier version, the reporting threshold in force and who acknowledged it.

environment.name: AirspaceClearance
environment.doc: Airspace authorities constrain when and where anything may fly; outside the cleared volume a drone does not watch.

environment.name: RadioInterference
environment.doc: A source of interference may degrade the mesh between drones as well as the link to the operations centre.

environment.name: SatellitePositioningOutage
environment.doc: Satellite positioning may be unavailable for minutes at a time; a drone then navigates by camera against stored maps.

environment.name: WeatherLimit
environment.doc: The swarm operates in weather up to moderate wind; above that it lands.

environment.name: FleetAndEnduranceBudget
environment.doc: Twelve drones, about 40 minutes of flight each, about 20 minutes of turnaround, 18 m/s cruise and about 3.0 km² under watch from altitude — the arithmetic coverage has to come out of.

environment.name: OperatorAttention
environment.doc: One operator can judge at most 20 alerts an hour and needs at least 30 seconds for each.

environment.name: ScopeExclusion
environment.doc: Weapons, interception and anything done to what is detected are out of scope: this system watches and reports.

environment.name: MeshRadio
environment.doc: The bearer of member-to-member coordination traffic, independent of the link to the operations centre — what lets the watch survive a ground-link drop.

environment.name: GroundStationLink
environment.doc: The radio link between the swarm and the ground station, not always available; the swarm works through a gap and reconciles afterwards.

environment.name: GroundStation
environment.doc: The fixed part of the system: tasking, watching, and in one architecture the coordinator that assigns sectors and rotations.

environment.name: RechargePointAndBatterySwap
environment.doc: The ground point and crew where batteries are swapped rather than charged in place, giving a 20-minute turnaround.

environment.name: RecoveryPoint
environment.doc: The point a drone that has lost contact with the swarm returns to on its own rather than becoming a hazard.

environment.name: StoredMaps
environment.doc: The reference imagery a drone navigates against when satellite positioning is unavailable.

environment.name: ClassifierRelease
environment.doc: One classifier version held across the fleet, with each drone's running version known.

capabilities.name: ContinuousAreaWatch
capabilities.doc: Hold continuous surveillance of the tasked area: at any moment at least one drone is watching each sector of it, through recharge rotations.

capabilities.name: DetectionClassificationAndReporting
capabilities.doc: Detect moving objects, classify them well enough to say whether they matter — saying Unknown rather than forcing a class — and report them with a position and a time.

capabilities.name: SwarmSelfCoordination
capabilities.doc: Settle sector handover, recharge rotation, coverage redistribution, deconfliction, relay, track correlation, track handover and member admission between the drones over the mesh.

capabilities.name: SupervisedCommandAndControl
capabilities.doc: Let one operator task, command, recall, watch and acknowledge for the whole swarm rather than fly each drone.

capabilities.name: DisconnectedOperationAndReconciliation
capabilities.doc: Keep detecting while cut off from the operations centre, hold the reports, and deliver them once the link is back — none lost.

capabilities.name: ReportTriageAndDecisionRecord
capabilities.doc: Triage reports before they reach the operator, merge duplicates, and keep a decision record for every report.

capabilities.name: GracefulDegradation
capabilities.doc: Keep flying and watching as drones leave, rejoin or are lost, with the loss of coverage bounded rather than the watch stopping.

capabilities.name: AirspaceComplianceAndSafeRecovery
capabilities.doc: Stay inside the cleared airspace, land safely when it is not available, and return to a recovery point when contact with the swarm is lost.

moes.name: areaUnderWatchFraction
moes.doc: The share of the area of interest under watch at any moment; the brief requires at least 0.9 and it is the first thing an architecture is judged on.

moes.name: watchEnduranceHoursWithoutPeople
moes.doc: How long the swarm holds the watch before it needs people to intervene. The brief names this as a thing that matters but states no number; 12 hours is set here by the architect as a working target and must be confirmed with the customer.

moes.name: reportDeliveryLatencySeconds
moes.doc: How old a report is when it reaches the operations centre with the link up; distinguishes architectures by where triage and correlation sit.

moes.name: positionErrorAfterGnssLossMetres
moes.doc: How accurately a drone knows where it is after ten minutes without satellite positioning; it sets where its reports place objects.

moes.name: coverageUnderMeshJammingFraction
moes.doc: The share of the area still under watch with half the links between drones jammed; the sharpest discriminator between ground-held and drone-held coordination.

moes.name: reportHoldDurationMinutes
moes.doc: How long a cut-off drone holds its reports without losing any before the link returns.

moes.name: missedDetectionFraction
moes.doc: The share of real objects that go undetected; with the false-alarm rate it fixes how much the reporting threshold can be tightened.

moes.name: falseAlarmsPerHour
moes.doc: False alarms reaching the operator each hour; traded against missed detections by the reporting threshold.

moes.name: alertsReachingOperatorPerHour
moes.doc: How many alerts actually reach the operator after triage and duplicate merging; an architecture that floods the operator fails whatever else it does.

moes.name: acknowledgedReportsThatMatterFraction
moes.doc: The share of the reports the operator acknowledges that turn out to matter; measures whether triage ranks the right things first.

moes.name: coverageDropAfterMemberLossFraction
moes.doc: How much coverage is lost when one drone is lost, before the remaining drones re-spread; the brief bounds it at 0.25.

moes.name: onboardClassifierCostUsdPerDrone
moes.doc: What the on-board computing for classification costs per drone; multiplied by twelve it decides whether classification can live on the drones at all.

moes.name: fleetSizeDrones
moes.doc: Twelve drones is the fleet the design has to work with — fixed by the brief, held as a requirement and never scored.

moes.name: memberFlightEnduranceMinutes
moes.doc: About 40 minutes of flight per drone, fixed by the brief. Transit out and back is spent from this same budget, so it is read together with the cruise-speed budget below, which the brief does give as 18 m/s.

moes.name: groundTurnaroundMinutes
moes.doc: About 20 minutes on the ground because batteries are swapped, not charged in place; with endurance it fixes the airborne share the fleet can hold.

moes.name: cruiseSpeedMetresPerSecond
moes.doc: About 18 m/s between recharge point and sector, fixed by the brief; without it nothing can say a drone reaches its station and returns inside its 40 minutes over an area several kilometres across.

moes.name: sensorFootprintSquareKilometres
moes.doc: About 3.0 km² under watch from a drone's watch altitude; this makes the coverage figure arithmetic rather than a hope.

moes.name: areaOfInterestSquareKilometres
moes.doc: The area of interest is up to 25 km², divided into sectors — fixed by the brief.

moes.name: operatorAlertCapacityPerHour
moes.doc: The most alerts one operator can judge in an hour; fixed by the brief as a property of the operator, not something an architecture improves.

moes.name: operatorSecondsPerAlert
moes.doc: The least time the operator needs for each alert; fixed by the brief and never scored.

moes.name: trackStaleThresholdSeconds
moes.doc: A track is stale once nothing has been seen for 120 seconds; the value the stale field of a Track is set from.

moes.name: gnssOutageToleratedMinutes
moes.doc: The satellite-positioning outage the position-error measure is stated against: ten minutes.

moes.name: jammedLinkShareFraction
moes.doc: The share of links between drones assumed jammed when the degraded-coverage measure is taken: half.

population.doc: Twelve identical small drones, each able to watch a sector for about forty minutes, which must settle sector handover, recharge rotation, coverage redistribution, deconfliction, relay, track correlation, track handover and admission with each other over a mesh radio that does not depend on the ground link.

coordinationFunctions.name: handOverSector
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone leaving to recharge hands its sector to one arriving, without a gap in the watch.

coordinationFunctions.name: rotateRecharge
coordinationFunctions.doc: The drones settle who goes to recharge next, so the airborne share never falls below what the sectors need.

coordinationFunctions.name: redistributeCoverage
coordinationFunctions.doc: When a drone is lost, the remaining ones re-spread over the sectors and the loss of coverage stays within its bound.

coordinationFunctions.name: deconflictFlight
coordinationFunctions.doc: The drones keep apart from each other in the air and at the recharge point.

coordinationFunctions.name: relayThroughNeighbour
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone out of range of the ground station passes its reports and status through a neighbour.

coordinationFunctions.name: correlateTracks
coordinationFunctions.doc: When two drones see the same object the swarm reports one track, not two.

coordinationFunctions.name: handOverTrack
coordinationFunctions.doc: When an object moves from one sector to the next, the drone watching the next sector takes over the track without losing it.

coordinationFunctions.name: admitMember
coordinationFunctions.doc: A drone joins the coordination only after the others have authenticated it; one that fails is quarantined until readmitted.

c2Functions.name: taskSurveillanceMission
c2Functions.doc: The operator gives the swarm the area, its sectors and the mission window.

c2Functions.name: issueSupervisoryCommand
c2Functions.doc: The operator sets priorities, points the swarm at a sector to look at more closely, and sets the reporting threshold — the least confidence a classification needs before it becomes a report.

c2Functions.name: recallToLand
c2Functions.doc: The operator recalls and lands the whole swarm or one drone, at any time.

c2Functions.name: presentStatusPicture
c2Functions.doc: The swarm shows where every drone is, what it is doing, how much coverage there is and what is degraded.

c2Functions.name: acknowledgeDetectionReport
c2Functions.doc: The operations centre confirms each detection report, so nothing is lost in a link gap.

hazards.name: PositionDriftHazard
hazards.doc: Without satellite positioning, a drone's position estimate drifts and its reports place objects in the wrong place.

hazards.name: MeshJammingHazard
hazards.doc: Interference cuts the links between drones, and coordination stalls.

hazards.name: MisclassificationHazard
hazards.doc: A detection is reported as the wrong class, or a forced class where Unknown was the truth.

hazards.name: SensingDegradedUnnoticedHazard
hazards.doc: A sensor degrades and nobody knows the reports from it are unreliable.

hazards.name: StaleTrackHazard
hazards.doc: A track is shown as current after nothing has seen the object for a while.

hazards.name: SpoofedMemberHazard
hazards.doc: Something that is not one of the drones joins the mesh and takes part in coordination.

hazards.name: MixedClassifierVersionsHazard
hazards.doc: Drones run different classifier versions and classify the same object differently.

hazards.name: OperatorOverloadHazard
hazards.doc: More alerts reach the operator than they can judge, and they accept what is in front of them.

rules.name: RecallWins
rules.doc: Once a drone is recalled, it does not watch again until it has landed.

rules.name: ReturnsWhenIsolated
rules.doc: From any situation a drone can be in, it can always get back to landed; an isolated drone included.

rules.name: GeofenceBreachEndsWatch
rules.doc: Once a drone is outside its cleared airspace, it does not watch until it has landed.

rules.name: QuarantinedStaysOut
rules.doc: Once a drone is quarantined, it takes no part in coordination until it has been readmitted.

modes.name: NavigationDegraded
modes.doc: The drone has no satellite positioning and navigates by what its camera sees against stored maps.

modes.name: SensingDegraded
modes.doc: The drone's sensors cannot be trusted as they are.

modes.name: Isolated
modes.doc: The drone is cut off from the other drones.

modes.name: Quarantined
modes.doc: The drone has failed admission and takes no part in coordination until readmitted.

modes.name: MeshDegraded
modes.doc: A share of the links between drones is jammed and the swarm coordinates over what is left.

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Where the detected object was, as the reporting drone estimated it.

fields.name: objectClass
fields.doc: One of the known classes, or Unknown when confidence is below the reporting threshold.

fields.name: confidence
fields.doc: How sure the classifier is of objectClass; compared against the reporting threshold in force.

fields.name: sensorId
fields.doc: Which sensor the detection came from, so a degraded sensor's reports can be found.

fields.name: classifierVersion
fields.doc: The classifier version that produced the class, so mixed versions across the fleet can be detected.

fields.name: ageSeconds
fields.doc: How long ago the detection was made, so a report held through a link gap is not read as current.

fields.name: trackId
fields.doc: The identity of the tracked object, one per object after correlation rather than one per observing drone.

fields.name: lastSeenTime
fields.doc: When anything last saw the object.

fields.name: stale
fields.doc: Set once nothing has been seen for the stale threshold — 120 seconds, a placeholder awaiting the customer's number.

rationale:
The brief describes a population, not a single system: twelve identical drones that settle eight named matters with each other over a mesh that is deliberately independent of the ground link. That independence is the whole point of the architecture decision, so the mesh peer port and its interface are declared in Common in the mandated shape and every member is wired through them from LA down; collapsing the swarm into one instance would make the decision unaskable. The operational entity the system takes over is one representative watch asset — today a crewed sortie flown to a sector under a duty controller's hand-made plan — which is why the controller's eight coordination activities become the coordination functions and the operations centre's five become the C2 functions.

Hazards, rules, modes and items are exactly those the brief names and no more: the eight known hazards go to SA::Hazards once and are satisfied by path below; the four rules are all carried by one member's state machine, since each is about what a single drone does after recall, geofence breach, isolation or quarantine; MeshDegraded is the only fleet-level mode. DetectionReport and Track carry exactly the fields the brief lists and nothing else, so a layer cannot quietly add an identifier to make its own life easier — acknowledgement therefore carries its own reference field and is documented as doing so.

On the measures: every target that the brief states is taken from the brief, and every number it marks as awaiting the customer is flagged as a placeholder so no report can claim a design has met a customer requirement. Three numbers the brief fixes rather than asks for — the fleet of twelve, the operator's 20 alerts an hour and 30 seconds each — are budgets, declared and never scored. The cruise speed is declared as a budget because the brief gives it (18 m/s) and because endurance and area alone cannot say whether a drone reaches its sector and returns: transit out and back is paid from the same forty minutes as the watching, and a model without the speed would let an architecture spend its whole flight budget on the return leg. Only watchEnduranceHoursWithoutPeople has a target nobody asked for; its doc says so.

Common holds definitions only, so it declares no state machines and no hazards of its own: modes, states and layer hazards belong where there are parts to carry and mitigate them. The ports declared here are the ones the layers will actually wire — mesh, ground link, operations link, airspace, ground service, sensor feed and navigation feed — so that the interfaces check does not report a port that connects to nothing.
